facts.text: Howell is the county seat of Livingston County. The city is mostly surrounded by Howell Township, but the two are administered separately.
The Howell Downtown Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1987, runs along five blocks of Grand River Avenue in the center of the city.
The historic district is mostly one and two story commercial buildings, in styles that range from Italianate and Richardsonian Romanesque to Neoclassical and Art Deco.
The Livingston County Courthouse at 200 East Grand River Avenue, completed in 1890 and topped by a central clock tower, is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
The Carnegie Library at 314 West Grand River Avenue is a Neoclassical building of local fieldstone and granite, topped by a round cupola and set on a large, park-like lot.
Howell's city parks include Lakeside Park on the north side of Thompson Lake and Scofield Park at Barnard and Thompson Streets, where a kayak launch was added at the beach in 2023.
Howell's major highways include Interstate 96, Business Loop I-96 and M-59.

The Howell Area Chamber of Commerce Foundation hosts the Fantasy of Lights Parade, which sends lighted floats down Grand River Avenue and has kicked off Howell's holiday season for 41 years. The 2026 parade is Friday, November 27.

christmas-light-installation.title: Christmas Light Installation in Howell, MI
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Christmas light installation in Howell, MI. Rooflines, tree wraps and shrubs, designed and hung by bucket-truck crews and taken down after the season.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Howell, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: A professionally lit home for the season, from the design to the takedown after the holidays. Rooflines, trees, shrubs and porches, hung straight and even.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: Howell opens the holidays with the Fantasy of Lights Parade, and in 2026 the floats roll down Grand River Avenue on Friday, November 27, the day after Thanksgiving. It is a natural moment to have your own house glowing, and worth planning around. We start at your home, not with a package. We look at the roofline, the peaks and the porch, which trees deserve a wrap, the shrubs along the walk and where the outlets are. Then we design a display sized to the house and your taste, from a simple warm white outline to a full front with wrapped trees. Once you approve the plan, we hang it, keep it shining all season and come back for it when the holidays end.
considerations: If you want your lights on for the Fantasy of Lights Parade, request your estimate well before November. Install season usually runs from October into early December, and the earliest requests have the most dates to choose from, which gives you the strongest shot at the timing you want.

Warm white gives a classic look that suits brick and older trim, while multicolor feels playful and nostalgic. Plenty of houses combine them, keeping the roofline warm white and putting the color in the trees. We talk through the options during the estimate, and the design follows your taste.
A plan for the whole front

The roofline is only part of the picture. A wrapped tree by the drive, lit evergreens along the foundation or a framed porch gives a display depth. We look at the whole front of the house during the estimate and suggest where light will do the most good.
faq: Do you put up Christmas lights for Howell homes?

Yes. Howell is within our Livingston County service area, and we also serve Howell Township, which mostly surrounds the city. Request an estimate here or call (248) 756-8915 to book a visit and talk through what you want.

We look over the house and yard, ask how you picture the finished display and note power and access. You then get a free written estimate detailing the scope: design, installation, in-season service and takedown once the holidays are over.
Do you take the lights down after the holidays?

Yes. Takedown after the season is part of our full service, so nobody in your house has to climb up in January. It is listed in your estimate along with the rest of the work, and we schedule it with you once the holidays have passed.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Howell, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Howell, MI commercial holiday lighting for Grand River storefronts, offices and managed properties, planned around historic facades. Free estimates.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Howell, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Facades traced in light, wrapped trees at the door and polished displays for offices, planned around Howell's architecture and hung from the bucket truck.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: Howell's downtown architecture does much of the work for you. The Howell Downtown Historic District runs five blocks along Grand River Avenue, a stretch of one and two story commercial buildings in Italianate, Richardsonian Romanesque, Neoclassical and Art Deco styles. Those cornices, arches and parapets are made to be outlined. When lighted floats travel Grand River Avenue for the Fantasy of Lights Parade, a storefront traced in light becomes part of the evening. We design commercial displays that follow the lines of each building, add wrapped trees or lit entries where they fit, and use bucket trucks for the elevated work. Offices, plazas and multi-tenant properties beyond downtown get the same careful design.
considerations: Richardsonian arches, Neoclassical columns and Art Deco verticals each call for a different outline. We plan runs that follow the strongest lines of your facade, so the building keeps its character at night instead of disappearing behind a curtain of lights.

The Fantasy of Lights Parade draws people to Grand River Avenue, and the 2026 parade is Friday, November 27. If you want your building lit for it, book early in the fall. Commercial work is typically scheduled from October into early December, and dates fill as the season approaches.

Professional offices and multi-tenant buildings usually want a polished look that never feels busy. We keep designs restrained where that suits the property, and a single written estimate takes the whole site from design through takedown.
faq: Do you light historic buildings in downtown Howell?

Yes. Historic facades are some of the most rewarding buildings to light. We plan the outline around the cornices, arches and trim, and treat older surfaces carefully. If an owner or landlord needs to sign off first, the written plan in your estimate makes that review straightforward.
Can several Grand River businesses coordinate?

Yes. Neighboring businesses, a downtown organization or a municipality can plan a consistent look across several buildings. Downtown and municipal lighting is one of our core services, and a shared plan keeps colors and spacing matched from one block to the next.
What does a commercial estimate look like?

We walk the property, review access and power, and talk through the look and the dates that matter to you. Afterward you receive a free written estimate listing the full scope, from the design to the takedown in the new year.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Christmas Lights in Howell, MI
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Permanent Christmas lights for Howell, MI homes, controlled by app all year. Holiday colors, game day themes and nightly accent light. Free estimates.
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: Install it once and light the house whenever you like. App-controlled roofline lighting for parade weekend, game days and ordinary evenings.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: Howell does the holidays in a big way, with the Fantasy of Lights Parade opening the season on Grand River Avenue. Permanent lighting lets your house join in without a yearly install. The lights go up along the roofline one time, and from then on your phone handles the rest. Choose warm white for December, deep orange for Halloween, green for St. Patrick's Day, your team's colors on game day, or a soft outline on any evening of the year. Schedules turn everything on and off for you. We plan the layout and the power, install everything and set up the app with you.
considerations: Worth it if you will use it

The value of permanent lighting grows with every night it is on. If your year includes Halloween, Independence Day, birthdays and game days, or you like a warm accent after dark, it is a strong fit. For a display you only want in December, seasonal installation may serve you better.

With seasonal lights, being lit for the Fantasy of Lights Parade means booking an install every fall. Permanent lighting is already on the roofline, so on parade night you choose a scene in the app and the house is ready. The same goes for any other evening you want it lit.

Where power is available shapes where the lights start and how the runs are split. We work that out on site before anything is ordered or installed, so the layout makes sense and the app controls the whole outline as one.
faq: Can you install permanent lighting on homes in Howell?

Yes. Howell is within our Livingston County service area for permanent lighting as well as seasonal displays. Request a free estimate, and we will check your roofline and outlets, talk through how you would use the lights and put the plan in writing.
How is it different from seasonal Christmas lights?

Seasonal lights go up in the fall and come down after the holidays. Permanent lighting stays on the roofline year-round and changes through the app, so you can use it for any holiday, game day or evening rather than a few weeks in winter.

It depends on where you live. If your home is part of an association, check its guidelines on exterior lighting and permanent fixtures before you commit. The written estimate describes the layout, which gives your board something specific to review.
